channel.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life
channel.description: The latest Essex news, sport and life, updated through the day.

image.title: The Seax: Essex news, sport and life

item.title: National Highways asks Thurrock to hold off on 200-home Grey Goose Farm scheme in Grays until February as residents object
item.description: Persimmon wants outline permission for homes north of Long Lane, but the roads agency says more modelling is needed on the busy North Stifford junction first.

item.title: Data centre and solar array proposed for contaminated former landfill at Little Canfield, near Dunmow
item.description: Crumps Estates Limited wants to build a 10,240 sq m data centre on the former Crumps Farm landfill, and two neighbouring parish councils have objected.

item.title: Plans that could see asylum seekers housed near Maldon raise concerns in a rural village
item.description: New plans could see asylum seekers housed in a rural village near Maldon, prompting local concerns, the Daily Gazette reports.

item.title: Underfloor heating firms pass £150,000 raised for Little Havens children's hospice in Thundersley over 18 years
item.description: Fastwarm and The Underfloor Heating Store have now signed up as platinum corporate members, pledging £10,800 a year between the three partners.

item.title: Wickford station's new ticket office opens as Greater Anglia rebuild nears the finish
item.description: Rayleigh and Wickford MP Mark Francois opened the ticket office on Monday, with the rest of the station upgrade due by the end of 2026.

item.title: Air ambulance charity draws more than 150 women to North Weald event on careers in emergency flight medicine
item.description: Essex & Herts Air Ambulance says women already make up about a third of its doctors and paramedics, well above the UK picture, and wants to go further.

item.title: Essex pair Jordan Cox and Sam Cook keep their places in England's Test squad for the South Africa tour
item.description: The two Essex players are among 15 picked by England for a three-Test series that starts in Johannesburg on 17 December.

item.title: Hidden faces, street drinking and e-scooters on footpaths could all bring fines in Harlow under council plans open until 5 January
item.description: Harlow Council wants residents' views on a package of Public Space Protection Orders, some town-wide and some for set places, with breaches punishable by fixed penalties or prosecution.

item.title: Essex families with children born in 2022-23 can now apply for reception places, with 15 January the deadline
item.description: Applications for primary school places starting in September 2027 are open online, and late forms are only looked at once on-time ones are settled.

item.title: Harwich lifeboat volunteers treat unconscious crew member on commercial ship before helicopter airlift
item.description: An injured sailor with head injuries was winched from a commercial vessel at Bawdsey anchorage and flown to Ipswich Hospital after Harwich RNLI was called out.

item.title: Government direction pushes Southend's draft local plan towards a six-week public consultation
item.description: The new plan would set the rules for where homes go and how the council handles applications for shared houses, affordable housing and hot food takeaways.

item.title: Auditors flag £1.7m pension difference in Southend's accounts but expect to finish on time
item.description: KPMG told councillors its audit of the 2025/26 accounts is on track, with work still under way on the value of council homes.

item.title: Tendring households can now recycle glass at the kerbside after 70,000 extra boxes go out
item.description: The council's environment lead told cabinet the expanded collections began on 5 October, and arts grants to the district have risen six-fold.

item.title: Brentwood's Chicken and Frog bookshop to shut, blaming steep rise in rates and power costs
item.description: The independent bookshop in Brentwood says sharp increases in its business rates and electricity bills have left it unable to carry on.

item.title: Chelmsford Chieftains hit nine to win 9-3 at Cardiff Fire
item.description: Tom Soar was man of the match as the Chieftains bounced back from Saturday's shootout loss at Swindon.

item.title: Chelmsford City hold leaders Ebbsfleet United to a 2-2 draw
item.description: Barnes scored twice for the National League South leaders, but the Clarets twice hit back in front of 1,390 fans.

item.title: Colchester United drawn at home to Mansfield Town in FA Cup second round
item.description: The U's will host Mansfield for a place in the third round, with ties to be played over the weekend of Saturday 5 December.

item.title: Southend's fenced-off Three Shells Lagoon should be removed and the beach restored, council report says
item.description: Southend-on-Sea City Council says taking out the failed lagoon is its preferred long-term option, and the proposal goes to Cabinet on 16 November.

item.title: Harlow's new bus lane and cycle corridor wins Partnership of the Year at the Essex Housing Awards
item.description: The Sustainable Transport Corridor along the A1019 from Burnt Mill to the town centre, finished in March with Homes England money, took the award for the Harlow and Gilston Garden Town partners.

item.title: Former teacher jailed for racist emails threatening Kemi Badenoch, MP for North West Essex
item.description: Kieran Kyle has been jailed after sending the Conservative leader emails that contained racist references and a threat to shoot her, according to reports of the court case.

item.title: Reform county councillor for Great Notley defends deleted immigration post as Braintree Conservatives demand he reflects
item.description: Carl Johnson, who sits on Essex County Council for Three Fields with Great Notley, says he stands by free speech after a Facebook post about who should hold elected office drew criticism.

item.title: Police still seeking witnesses to Sunday's early-hours crash that killed two people on Chelmsford's Copperfield Road
item.description: Essex Police wants doorbell, dashcam and eyewitness accounts after a driver and passenger died when their Ford Fiesta struck a property wall near Havisham Way.

item.title: Basildon Council takes back three homes in St Martin's, Billericay West and Lee Chapel North after serious tenancy breaches
item.description: The council's antisocial behaviour team and Essex Police worked together to recover the properties, which will be repaired and relet to households in need.

item.title: Harlow man, 19, charged with taking a vehicle without consent and failing to stop for police
item.description: Freddie Selby, of Radburn Close, Harlow, is due at Chelmsford Magistrates' Court on 17 November and has been released on conditional bail.

item.title: Harlow college shut over building safety fears wins approval for a permanent new school
item.description: Sir Frederick Gibberd College pupils have been taught in temporary classrooms for two years after the modular main building was closed.

item.title: Maldon council says national rules leave little room to refuse new homes in Tollesbury, Great Totham and Latchingdon
item.description: The district's leader says unpopular village schemes cannot be turned down without sound planning evidence, as a new national scheme also takes many decisions away from committee.

item.title: Harlow man banned for 30 months after admitting driving at more than three times the limit on Southern Way
item.description: Krysztof Szwaczka, 42, of Longbanks, Harlow, admitted drink-driving an Audi in March and was given a curfew and unpaid work.

item.title: Multi-agency raids on more than 100 Essex premises seize £10,360 in cash and illicit cigarettes
item.description: Operation Machinize, coordinated by the National Crime Agency and carried out locally by Essex Police with partner agencies, targeted organised crime linked to businesses across the county.

item.title: Basildon mayor urges council to complete war memorial championed by late D-Day veteran Don Sheppard
item.description: A motion asks officers to find a prominent town centre site and cost a memorial the 104-year-old veteran campaigned for before his death in 2024.

item.title: Southend council still heading for a £12m overspend as one child's care placement tops £1m a year
item.description: The latest six-month forecast shows the gap narrowing by about £1.3m, but children's social care costs have climbed by around £1.5m since the summer.

item.title: Harlow Council asks residents whether the town is on the right track in its 2026 survey
item.description: Harlow Council has opened its 2026 residents' survey, asking people for their views on the direction the town is heading, Your Harlow reports.

item.title: Three Kent men charged over suspected hare coursing near Bardfield
item.description: Johnny Powell, 22, of Lenham Heath, Joseph King, 22, of Offham, and William Cook, 37, of Longfield, are due at Southend Magistrates' Court on Wednesday 11 November.

item.title: Braintree and County Hall leaders vow to resist Home Office bid to keep Wethersfield asylum site open after April 2027
item.description: The government has applied to extend its use of the former airbase near Braintree, where asylum seekers have been housed since July 2023, and both councils say they will look at ways to oppose it.

item.title: Southend aims to bring council home repairs up to industry norms by Christmas after regulator judgement
item.description: Electrical safety checks on council homes are now close to complete, but councillors heard that repairs remain the weak spot in Southend's response to the social housing regulator.

item.title: Three in four Thurrock children entering care now get their first health check on time, up from 36%
item.description: Councillors scrutinising children's services heard that initial health assessments within the 20-day legal deadline have more than doubled.

item.title: Epping Forest councillors asked to back raising the top fly-tipping fine from £1,000 to £5,000
item.description: A motion to full council called for the district's maximum fixed penalty for fly-tipping to rise fivefold now that the law allows it.

item.title: Tendring set to adopt new protection plans for St Osyth and Manningtree and Mistley conservation areas
item.description: Cabinet will decide on 13 November whether to adopt the final two of 20 conservation area appraisals, including revised boundaries.

item.title: Tendring adopts new skills and conduct standards for council housing staff after tenant feedback
item.description: Cabinet adopted a policy setting out the skills, qualifications and conduct expected of housing staff, to meet a new regulator standard.

item.title: Isthmian Premier: Maldon & Tiptree win 3-1 at Wingate & Finchley as Aveley are beaten 4-0 at Ramsgate
item.description: A mixed Saturday for the Essex clubs in the Isthmian Premier Division, with one away win, two draws and a heavy defeat on the Kent coast.

item.title: Free football pilot for 10 to 13-year-olds runs at Orsett Heath Academy in Grays
item.description: Basildon-based Windy Sport Group is offering free, limited places on its Windy Active Kids sessions for boys and girls not signed to a professional academy, with online registration required.

item.title: Historian calls for Grays church memorial naming 22 boys lost in the 1875 Goliath training ship fire
item.description: Peter Valentine wants plaques at St Peter and St Paul's Church in Grays, 150 years after the disaster on the ship moored nearby.

item.title: Police seek doorbell and dash cam footage after young driver dies in Harlow crash at Kingsland
item.description: The man in his 20s was alone in a Ford Fiesta that hit a parked car shortly after 5.30am on Sunday, police said, and the road has since reopened.

item.title: Braintree Town beaten 4-1 by Weston-super-Mare in National League South
item.description: Luke Coulson struck twice before half-time for the hosts at the Optima Stadium, and Hubbard's late goal was only a consolation for the Iron.

item.title: Colchester United edge Worcester City 1-0 to reach the FA Cup second round
item.description: Danny Cowley's U's beat the non-league visitors at the JobServe Community Stadium on Saturday to stay in the competition.

item.title: Chelmsford Chieftains lose 6-5 to Swindon Wildcats 2 after a shootout
item.description: Sasha Maltsev was named man of the match after scoring twice, including a shorthanded goal, at the Link Centre in West Swindon.

item.title: Isthmian North: Buckhurst Hill win 3-0 at Bowers & Pitsea as Witham Town triumph at Redbridge
item.description: Two away wins for Essex clubs headlined Saturday in the Isthmian North, while Takeley and Little Oakley were both beaten 1-0 at home.

item.title: Elliot Long double earns Billericay Town a 2-2 draw at Dagenham & Redbridge
item.description: Danny Scopes' side twice found the net through their striker and held on for a point against the Daggers in the National League South.

item.title: Colchester A12 death: witnesses sought after young man is struck near junction 26 on Saturday evening
item.description: The collision near junction 26 shortly before 5.30pm on Saturday closed both carriageways until shortly before 5am on Sunday.

item.title: Chelmsford City come from behind to beat Farnborough 2-1
item.description: Goals from Clarke and a Barham penalty turned the game around at the Dunmow Group Community Stadium after Max Ehmer had put the visitors ahead.

item.title: Candle fire spreads through roof and leaves two Colchester homes uninhabitable
item.description: Working smoke alarms on both floors helped residents get out when a bedroom fire started by a candle spread into the roof space and the house next door on Saturday afternoon.

item.title: Man and woman from Tilbury charged with cannabis supply and criminal property offences
item.description: Two people from Canberra Square, Tilbury, have been charged after a warrant was executed at an address on 2 November, and are due at Basildon Crown Court on 4 December.

item.title: Tendring budgets for life beyond 2028 as the government pauses the council shake-up
item.description: With Whitehall reviewing its plan to replace Essex's councils, Tendring's cabinet has agreed to plan four years ahead, and backed money for toilets, playgrounds and housing staff.

item.title: Thurrock's special needs funding gap keeps growing as Treetops School plans 110 more places
item.description: Children's services are on course to underspend by about £0.5m, but the grant that pays for special educational needs is heading deeper into deficit, councillors heard.

item.title: Thurrock picked as one of seven national pilots helping children stay with their wider family
item.description: The Kinship Zones pilot will give practical, emotional and financial support to relatives raising children, as Thurrock reshapes its children's social care.

item.title: Southend's fraud investigators have brought in more than £800,000 for the council this year
item.description: School admissions fraud and Blue Badge misuse were among the areas councillors raised as the council's counter fraud team reported on its work.

item.title: Man, 32, jailed for 58 weeks for breaching restraining order in Colchester area
item.description: Shane Furner, of no fixed address, admitted breaching an order that barred him from contacting a victim and from going to an address in the Colchester area.

item.title: Elliott Smith named Brentwood Sports Personality of the Year
item.description: Brentwood Central Boxing Club was named Community Club of the Year at a joint awards night with Rochford, with Graham Gooch helping to present.

item.title: Dispersal order covers Witham town centre until 6pm on Sunday
item.description: Essex Police has dispersal powers in place across Witham town centre and nearby roads from 6pm on Friday 6 November to 6pm on Sunday 8 November to tackle anti-social behaviour.

item.title: Southend mark 20 years since Eastwood sank Manchester United, as Sam Austin rejoins Kidderminster on loan
item.description: BBC Essex revisits the night Roots Hall beat Sir Alex Ferguson's side in the League Cup, while forward Sam Austin heads back to Aggborough for the rest of the season.

item.title: Thurrock's war memorials tidied and replanted ahead of Remembrance Sunday
item.description: Council officers, ward councillors and local forums have painted, planted and cleared around memorials in Tilbury, Grays, Aveley, Purfleet and East Tilbury.
